messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testContainsIgnoreCase_LocaleIndependence` aims to verify that `StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase` functions correctly and consistently across different locales, especially locales with specific case transformation rules like Turkish ("tr"). The test sets the default locale to different values and checks if `containsIgnoreCase` returns expected results for pairs of strings involving case differences.

The implementation of `containsIgnoreCase` is:
```java
public static boolean containsIgnoreCase(String str, String searchStr) {
    if (str == null || searchStr == null) {
        return false;
    }
    return contains(str.toUpperCase(), searchStr.toUpperCase());
}
```
This means `containsIgnoreCase` converts both strings to uppercase using the default locale (implicitly, because `String.toUpperCase()` method without locale argument uses the default JVM locale), then calls `contains`.

The bug report summary reports a known problem that `String.toUpperCase()` (and related case conversion methods) are locale-sensitive, which is usually not intended behavior in case-insensitive comparisons. Case conversions in some locales, like Turkish, yield different uppercase results (e.g., "i".toUpperCase() = "İ" with dot in Turkish locale vs "I" in English/US).

Thus, when the test changes the default locale to Turkish, the uppercase conversion in `containsIgnoreCase` produces different results than expected, causing the test assertion to fail.

Proper case-insensitive string comparison should use a locale-neutral or fixed locale case conversion (like `Locale.ENGLISH`) or use `toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)`/`toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)` to ensure consistent uppercase transformation regardless of the system locale.

This explains why the test `testContainsIgnoreCase_LocaleIndependence` fails: the use of `toUpperCase()` without specifying a locale caused locale-dependent behavior, breaking the expected results in the Turkish locale.

No other recent bug reports are directly relevant apart from the current report mentioning this specific problem of locale-sensitive string case handling.

Suggested fix is to change the implementation of `containsIgnoreCase` so that the case conversion is locale-independent by using e.g. `str.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)` and `searchStr.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)`.

This will make `containsIgnoreCase` behave consistently regardless of the default locale and fix the test failure.

---
